title: Assignment 2: Google Trends
text:
Google Trends in R
I used the provided gtrendsR script to reproduce the Google Trends query in R. I worked from the first successful pull because repeated requests can be rate-limited.

library(gtrendsR)
library(readr)

TrumpHarrisElection <- gtrends(
  c("Trump", "Harris", "election"),
  onlyInterest = TRUE,
  geo = "US",
  gprop = "web",
  time = "today+5-y",
  category = 0
)

the_df <- TrumpHarrisElection$interest_over_time

plot(TrumpHarrisElection)

For the final plot, I used the CSV saved from my successful R pull.

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

the_df <- read_csv(
  "gtrends_us_5y_2026-09-15.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

the_df$date <- as.Date(the_df$date)
the_df$hits_num <- parse_number(as.character(the_df$hits))

ggplot(
  the_df,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = hits_num,
    color = keyword
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Google Trends Interest Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Relative Search Interest",
    color = "Search Term"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

title: Assignment 2: Google Trends
text:
Comparison
I also ran the same R query twice. In my test, the two interest_over_time data frames were identical. However, Google Trends uses sampled data, so repeated pulls are not guaranteed to always match.
The website and R methods use the same Google Trends source, but they are not identical in how the query is recorded and reproduced. The website method requires the user to manually record the search terms, geography, time window, category, and search type. In R, those choices are written directly into the code, which makes the query easier to reproduce and scale.
The R approach is also more practical when working with many search terms or countries because the same code can be modified and rerun. The website method is easier for a small number of searches, but it becomes more time-consuming as the number of queries increases.
The assignment also compares the search terms “Harris” and “Kamala Harris.” These are not the same concept because “Harris” can refer to many different people, places, and organizations. This shows that the exact search term matters when using Google Trends as a measure of public interest.
I also ran the same R query twice. In my test, the two interest_over_time data frames were identical. However, Google Trends uses sampled search data, so identical results in one test do not guarantee that every future pull will return exactly the same values. The R method provides better reproducibility and is easier to scale, while the website method is simpler for quick manual searches.

title: Website Design Note
text:
I created this website using RStudio and Quarto and published it through GitHub Pages. Since this was my first time building a website this way, I wanted to keep the design simple and easy to manage. I also wanted it to look professional enough to use for school and future academic work.
For the overall appearance, I chose the Litera theme because I liked how clean and readable it looked. On the homepage, I used the Jolla layout because I liked the way it placed the profile image and introduction together. I also included a short bio, my research interests, and links to my email and GitHub so the main information is easy to find.
The navigation bar includes Home, Research, Teaching, CV, and Assignments. I separated the pages this way so the website would not feel too crowded. The Research page is still fairly simple because I have not completed a class research project yet, but I plan to update it as the semester continues. I also included a Teaching page so I have a place to add teaching-related experience in the future. The CV page includes a PDF copy of my résumé that can be viewed directly on the site or downloaded.
One part of the process that took some trial and error was figuring out how Quarto, RStudio, and GitHub Pages work together. I learned that the Quarto files are edited in RStudio, then the website has to be rendered so the updated HTML files are created in the docs folder. Those files are then uploaded to GitHub, where GitHub Pages publishes the live version of the website.
I wanted the site to be straightforward and flexible rather than overly complicated. I plan to continue updating it as I complete more assignments, research projects, and other academic work.
